site.name: Coldshift Dash
site.tagline: a car dashboard for old and new Android phones
site.description: Coldshift Dash turns an Android phone in your car into a dashboard: offline maps and navigation, a dashcam, your music, the engine's readings, a log book and Convoy, for phones from Android 4.4 on. Free and open source.
site.pitch: The phone in your dash, as your dash.
site.hero: Offline maps and navigation, a dashcam, your music, the engine's readings and a log book, on one screen made for a glance. It runs on the phone you already have, even one from 2014, and needs no account and no internet.

screens.caption: Maps: the route, the next turn and the others in the convoy
Media: the music on the card, folder by folder
Dashcam: recording, with a moment marked
Convoy: who's ahead, who's behind, and the messages
Engine: readings from an OBD2 adapter

features.name: Maps and navigation
features.text: Offline maps of your region in a quiet, dark style made to glance at, heading-up or north-up. Hold a point, search a place or address, or pick Home: the route is worked out on the phone, with the next turn, spoken prompts, rerouting and arrival.

features.name: Dashcam
features.text: Records in a loop at 1080p or 720p, with the speed and position saved beside each clip. Mark a moment as you drive, lock a clip to keep it, and set how much of the card clips may use.

features.name: Your music
features.text: Plays the music on the phone's card, folder by folder with their covers, shuffle and repeat, and keeps playing behind the map.

features.name: Engine
features.text: Revs, speed, temperatures, boost, lambda and more from a Bluetooth OBD2 adapter, on two pages; fault codes in plain words, and a Diagnostics page with the check-engine light and the readiness monitors.

features.name: Log book
features.text: Trips log themselves. A stop at a fuel station offers to log the fill-up, the odometer keeps itself up to date, service reminders come due, and business trips go into a travel logbook for SARS.

features.name: Track
features.text: Drive a stretch of road once to record it, as a lap or point to point. Later runs are timed against your best with a live gap, and a run can be saved as a dashcam clip.

features.name: Convoy
features.text: Cars driving together see each other on the map, with quick messages and push-to-talk voice notes. Join with a QR code; no account.

features.name: Your car's own look
features.text: Each car gets its own look: its name, badges, background, colours and its picture on the map. The settings back up and restore, so a new phone picks up where the old one left off.

steps: Download the APK on the phone and open it.
When Android asks, allow installing apps from your browser or files app.
Choose Install, then open Coldshift Dash and allow what it asks for: location, camera, microphone, files and notifications.
apks.name: Android 6 and later
apks.detail: For current phones (Android 6 to 16), if you'd rather not use Google Play
apks.note: It asks for All files access, to read the maps and music in the coldshift.dash folder on the phone's card.

steps: On the phone, turn on Settings, Security, Unknown sources.
Download the APK on the phone, open it from the notification and choose Install.
Or from a computer: adb install -r dash-legacy.apk
apks.name: Android 4.4
apks.detail: For older phones on Android 4.4 KitKat, such as a Huawei Ascend G7
apks.note: Made for a phone that lives in the car: kiosk mode starts it with the phone and keeps it in front.

downloads.desktop: A desktop companion, to put maps and music on the phone, is coming.
